turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Use these continual harness prompt notes, memories, skills, and subagent specs when they are relevant. The base system prompt is immutable; prompt entries below are supplemental notes only.

Keep `await refine.run()` continual harness edits small and evidence-backed.

Use `<skill_import> ...` in shell when a CLI exists. Continual harness skill entries are Python REPL skills with an explicit Python `reference` and `arguments` contract. Spawn a continual harness subagent spec by composing a concise task prompt and calling `handle = await rlm.spawn('sub-task', name='worker')`; admission returns immediately with `rlm_child_id`, `name`, `session_dir`, and `model`, never the child's answer. Results arrive only through explicit `agent_message` replies or files; children reply with `await agent_message.send(message, receiver_role='parent')`. Use `await rlm.list_subagents()` to recover direct child handles and `await agent_message.send(..., receiver_role='child', receiver_name=handle.name)` for follow-ups. Do not invent wrappers such as `call_skill(...)`, `run_subagent(...)`, or named subagent registries.

steps.output: [('arc_motif_replication_task_family', 'ARC motif replication task family', 'ARC task family seen in Continual-ARC: sparse target-colored cells plus a small multicolor motif/template; outputs replicate the motif around each target. Demonstrations established target alignment can be identified by matching a distinctive template anchor: vertical [8,1,1] replicated with target aligned to middle 1; horizontal [8,3,9] with target aligned to center 3; vertical [0,0,3] with target aligned to center 0. Other demos show more complex motifs including background-colored cells within a bounding box, so carefully infer which cells are copied and anchor before stamping. Generate output with Python and validate row/column dimensions before submitting; several manual grid constructions here were malformed or wrong. For the e903b660 test, there were scattered 1 targets and a 3x3 source arrangement [4,5,5;8,5,8;8,5,0], centered around 5, but naïve centered replication attempts failed; likely anchor/template interpretation more nuanced.'), ('arc_collinear_gap_fill', 'ARC collinear gap filling with color 3', 'Continual-ARC pattern: sparse marker cells among a background; connect aligned consecutive markers with color 3. For each row and each column, find marker cells (non-background); between consecutive markers along that line, recolor intervening background cells to 3. Preserve all original markers and other cells; horizontal and vertical fills can overlap. A solved task with varying grid/background/marker colors used exactly this rule. Sparse unaligned markers can yield no changes. Avoid blanket recoloring.'), ('arc_split_panel_cellwise_match', 'ARC split-panel cellwise match', 'Continual-ARC task family: input split into two aligned panels by a solid separator (vertical or horizontal). Output has the panel dimensions. Compare corresponding cells in both panels: output uses color 3 where the cells are equal; elsewhere use the shared/background comparison color. Demonstrations support: Demo 2 top/bottom panels of 8/9 and 4/9 produced background 9 with 3 exactly at positions where both panels were 9. Demo 3 left panel mostly 5 with sparse 4 and right panel 5/6 produced output background 5 and 3 at cells where both panels were 5. Demo 4 left 9/6 vs right 6/4 produced background 6 and 3 where both panels were 6. Demo 5 left 6/0 vs right 6/1 produced 3 at matching 6/6 positions, background 6. Avoid incorrectly marking all sparse cells from one panel alone. For horizontal test panel alignment, output likely 12x13; match cells (top 7 with lower 7) should become 3 and all others use 7 as matching/background color.'), ('arc_background_to_foreground_color_inversion', 'ARC background-to-foreground color inversion', 'Continual-ARC demonstrated transformation: for a grid with uniform background color B and sparse foreground color F, output replaces every B cell with F and every original F cell with 0, keeping dimensions and positions. Demo: 5 background/4 marks became 4 background/0 marks. Applied to test: 5→9, 9→0. Use this rule when demos show this exact mapping; do not assume unrelated sparse-marker tasks use it.'), ('arc_marker_guided_motif_replication', 'ARC marker-guided motif replication', 'Continual-ARC task pattern: A multicolor template object appears among uniform background and one or more identical marker cells (e.g. color 5). Copy the entire template shape/colors to each marker location, preserving original template and background. Align marker to template bounding-box center cell (for odd 3x3 template, internal offset (1,1)); translate all template non-background cells by marker_coord - center_coord. Clip cells outside grid; markers are overwritten by copied template. Demonstrations: 23x11 background 8, object color 3 occupying rows15-19 cols3-5 with a 4x3 block plus tail at (19,5); 5 markers at (2,8),(9,2),(19,9). Output copies aligned by template bounding-box center (relative (2,1)) to each 5. Current task: 3x3 object rows2-4 cols7-9, copy offset center to 5 at (3,1),(6,4). Preserve original. Be careful top row may have only one nonbackground cell; clipping and offsets matter.'), ('arc_noise_grid_motif_replication_by_zero_pattern_matches', 'ARC noise-grid motif replication by zero-pattern matches', "Continual-ARC task family: Grid has a noisy two-color background (e.g. 0/8) and a small connected motif of a third color. The output preserves the grid except it overlays copies of the motif color at all translated placements where every motif cell aligns with a background 0 (the motif coordinates are taken relative to its bounding-box top-left). For each valid placement, recolor those matched 0 cells to motif color. Overlapping copies form the union. Existing motif seed remains. Identify the motif's exact colored-cell offsets from the seed; scan all translations whose motif offsets land on zeros, paint those offsets. Demonstrated with motifs 2x3 and irregular shapes; successful application yielded correct output. Do not replicate at every zero anchor: only placements where all motif-offset cells in source grid are zero."), ('arc_horizontal_stripe_trailing_gap_coloring', 'ARC horizontal stripe trailing-gap coloring', "Continual-ARC task-cdae771b: grids with horizontal bars/stripes on uniform background. Demo 2 had a color-9 run ending at column 16 followed by two color-8 background cells; those two cells became 1. Demo 1 also added 1s on the shorter repeated stripe motif's right-side tail. Useful distinction: color the trailing gap with 1, do not extend the marker color. Specific applicability should be checked from pattern context."), ('unresolved_noisy_background_motif_copy_arc_family', 'Unresolved noisy-background motif-copy ARC family', 'Task family evidence from task-37a30187.
